summary: 成帝养子继位，欲强主威而限田夺权皆败，宠董贤，终使王莽乘隙再起。
summary_en: Adopted by Emperor Cheng, he tried to strengthen the throne with land limits and power grabs, all in vain; his favor for Dong Xian let Wang Mang rise again.

portrait.appearance_basis: 《汉书》未系统描写哀帝形貌。画像宜表现年少而欲有为、终溺私宠的君主之态，衣冠从西汉末制度。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 为定陶王

timeline.title: 立为太子
timeline.summary: 成帝立定陶王欣为太子。
timeline.summary_en: Emperor Cheng made Xin, king of Dingtao, heir apparent.

timeline.title: 诏议限田
timeline.summary: 师丹等议限田宅奴婢，未果。
timeline.summary_en: Shi Dan and others proposed limits on fields, houses, and slaves; nothing came of it.

timeline.title: 改号陈圣刘太平皇帝等
timeline.summary: 夏贺良等言改元易号，旋罢。
timeline.summary_en: Xia Heliang and others urged a change of era and title; the change was soon rescinded.

timeline.title: 董贤贵幸
timeline.summary_en: Dong Xian's favor exceeded that of any minister.

timeline.title: 策免三公求直言
timeline.summary: 日食等灾异后策免丞相孔光等，下诏求直言。
timeline.summary_en: After eclipses and other portents he dismissed Chancellor Kong Guang and others and sought plain speech.

timeline.title: 匈奴单于来朝
timeline.summary_en: The Wuzhuliu chanyu came to court.

timeline.title: 王莽再起
timeline.summary: 王政君遣使迎莽，董贤自杀。
timeline.summary_en: Empress Dowager Wang summoned Wang Mang back; Dong Xian killed himself.

timeline.summary_en: He died without issue; Jizi of Zhongshan was brought in as heir (Emperor Ping).

bio_md:
# 汉哀帝 · 主要事迹

刘欣是[[han-cheng-di|成帝]]的养子，本为定陶王，绥和元年入继为太子，次年成帝暴崩，即位。哀帝年少而欲有为，一上台就想革除王氏外戚把持朝政的积弊——然而六年之间，改革尽成泡影，汉家国祚反而加速滑向王莽。

哀帝朝的大事，件件指向「强主威」而件件落空：即位初诏议限田限奴婢，师丹等议之而卒不行，贵族豪强的反弹使限田令胎死腹中；建平二年听信夏贺良等改元易号，闹出「陈圣刘太平皇帝」的笑话，旋又自罢；为压王氏之势，他扶植祖母傅氏、母亲丁氏一族与董贤，结果董贤宠极人臣，「断袖」之宠名传千古，而主威愈弱。

元寿二年，乌珠留单于入朝，是西汉末年少有的一次四夷来朝的体面场面；同年六月，哀帝崩，无子。太皇太后王政君即日收回玺绶，召[[xin-wang-mang|王莽]]入宫，董贤自杀。史赞谓哀帝「睹孝成之世，禄去公室，欲强主威，而丁、傅、董贤乱之」——他不是没有振作的念头，只是西汉的制度病已入膏肓，非一君之力所能救。

> 参考：点校本《汉书》卷011《哀帝纪》、《佞幸传》、《食货志》，谭图第 2 册。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Xin, the adopted heir of

, had been king of Dingtao; he entered the succession in the first Suihe year and took the throne when Cheng died the next year. Young and eager to act, he meant from the start to break the grip of the Wang consorts on the government — yet in six years every reform came to nothing, and the Han mandate slid faster toward Wang Mang.

Each great matter of his reign aimed at "strengthening the sovereign" and each failed: on accession he ordered a debate on limiting fields and slaves; Shi Dan's proposals died in the face of aristocratic opposition. In the second Jianping year he let Xia Heliang and others persuade him to change era and title, producing the farce of "the Chengsheng Liu Taiping emperor," soon rescinded. To counter the Wangs he raised his grandmother's Fu clan, his mother's Ding clan, and above all Dong Xian — whose favor exceeded all precedent, the "severed sleeve" infatuation passing into proverb, while the throne's authority only weakened.

In the second Yuanshou year the Wuzhuliu chanyu came to court, one of the last dignified scenes of four-tribes homage in Western Han; in the sixth month of that year Ai died without issue. The grand empress dowager Wang Zhengjun took back the seal the same day, summoned

into the palace, and Dong Xian killed himself. The historians' eulogy: "Having seen in the reign of Cheng the offices drained from the royal house, he wished to strengthen the sovereign's authority — but the Dings, the Fus, and Dong Xian disordered it." He was not without the will to reform; the institutional disease of Western Han was simply past cure by any single ruler.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, ch. 11 (Benji of Emperor Ai), the biography of the Favorites, and the Treatise on Food and Money; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2.
